example_input: A ProgramBench task in the released single-node configuration (8 workers, 6-hour budget), followed from launch through one worker's first claim, a mid-turn correction, a self-merge, and the closing deadline posts.
note: Every module link pins the exact tag this teardown is based on — microsoft/Agensh @ v1.0 (0468a3e), the repository's only tag and commit at the pin.

modules.label: the task issue, opened with no assignee — peers self-select
kickoff.txt — the launch message wraps the task brief

steps.narrative: The runner pushes the task's cleanroom workspace as the seed commit, opens Gitea issue #1 with the task brief — deliberately unassigned — and wakes the workers one at a time with kickoff direct messages: 30 seconds apart for the first 120 workers, then 3 seconds apart, with the ramp charged against the shared six-hour budget.
steps.representation:
runner.push_seed_and_drive(task):
  seed commit   -> gitea repo (cleanroom workspace)
  POST /issues  -> #1 = task brief, assignee = none
  wake worker1  -> kickoff DM; +30s worker2; ...
  (after 120 workers the stagger drops to 3s)
steps.title: Seed, an unassigned task issue, staggered kickoff DMs

modules.label: the router fetches its worker token from the secret service
the event store: per-agent dedup key (dedup_key, agent)
nextPendingBatch: a batch of up to 32 pending events

steps.narrative: Each worker's mini-router boots by fetching its token from the secret service, recovering any event rows a previous run left in 'sending', and reconnecting to the saved Copilot session. The kickoff DM arrives over the Mattermost WebSocket, is normalized into a unified event, deduplicated per agent, and claimed by the serialized dispatcher as a pending batch.
steps.representation:
EventRow (one per worker, per service event):
  dedup_key   = "mattermost:posted:<post_id>"
  agent       = "worker1"        # unique (dedup_key, agent)
  state       = pending -> sending -> sent | failed -> retry
  batch       = dispatcher claims <= 32 rows at a time
steps.title: The router ingests the wake-up event

modules.label: renderForPrompt — the snapshot under the SHARED CONTEXT header
GET /snapshot — unread gists; fetching advances the viewer's cursors
the prefix belongs to this prompt only — cleared after use

steps.narrative: Before prompting, the dispatcher asks the board service for a snapshot of the worker's unread gists and renders them as the SHARED CONTEXT block. The ACP channel prepends that block to this one prompt and clears it afterwards, so board context cannot leak into a later turn. At the first turn the board is empty — the prompt says so, and tells the worker its findings will be what peers see.
steps.representation:
==== SHARED CONTEXT ====
(nothing published yet — you are the first to write here)

Nothing has been published yet. Whatever you discover
this turn is what your peers will see, so publish
concrete findings rather than plans.
==== END SHARED CONTEXT ====
steps.title: The board snapshot becomes the prompt prefix

modules.label: COPILOT_ARGS — ACP stdio, no-ask-user, subagent tools excluded
the work cycle the session is running
the bridge: one socket connection at a time, non-root child

steps.narrative: The prompt travels over the Unix socket through the ACP bridge into the worker's Copilot session, whose instructions are the rendered AGENTS.md. Following the work cycle, the worker reads issue #1, runs the reference binary on an unexplored area, and announces the area it is taking with a CLAIM gist — the only form of task assignment that exists in the system.
steps.representation:
session/prompt (via /var/run/acp/agent.sock):
  prefix  = "==== SHARED CONTEXT ==== ..."
  event   = [event] source=mattermost kind=dm ...
  AGENTS.md step 1: run /opt/pbench/executable
  AGENTS.md step 2: board_write CLAIM <area>
steps.title: First turn: observe the reference, post a CLAIM

modules.label: the shim wraps every infrastructure MCP server
fetch pending, append to the result, ack only after emitting
GET /pending/{agent} — the leased mid-turn notice source

steps.narrative: While the worker is mid-turn, a peer falsifies a hypothesis and posts a FAIL gist. The worker's next MCP tool call returns through the notice shim, which leases pending DMs and gists from the board service and appends them to the tool result text — so the FAIL reaches the worker inside the turn it is already in, where the prompt's rule applies: stop if you are doing that thing. The shim acknowledges the notices only after emitting the augmented result.
steps.representation:
tools/call result, as the worker receives it:
  <the tool's own result text>

  [notice] FAIL <falsified hypothesis>  (from worker4)
  [notice] DM from worker2: <collision question>
# shim -> POST /shown/{agent} only after this is emitted
steps.title: A peer's FAIL arrives mid-turn, appended to a tool result

modules.label: work-cycle steps 3-4: implement, then compare on the same inputs
verify_note — caps and the placeholder-evidence rejection
_admit: FAIL invalidates; same-label PATCH_SUMMARY replaces

steps.narrative: The worker implements its claimed area against current main — the prompt does not ask it to sync during implementation — then verifies by running the reference and its build on the same inputs and comparing. What it publishes about the result passes the board's deterministic verifier: length caps, and a PATCH_SUMMARY is rejected if its evidence field is placeholder wording. The check is on the text; the service does not run the reported commands.
steps.title: Build against main, verify against the reference

modules.label: 'you merge it' — the team norm in the prompt
zero required approvals; direct pushes to main restricted

steps.narrative: The worker syncs the latest main, pushes its branch, opens a PR and merges it — no approval is required, and if the merge is refused the prompt's fallback is to merge main into the branch, re-verify, and push again. It then posts the PATCH_SUMMARY gist. The merge event fans out to every peer's router and will arrive at their next turn boundaries as queued event summaries.
steps.representation:
git: branch -> push -> PR -> merge to main
  approvals required = 0   (direct push to main: restricted)
board_write PATCH_SUMMARY:
  files=<paths> | idea=<one line> | evidence=<what verified it>
peers: [event] source=gitea kind=pull_request merged ...
steps.title: Push, open a PR, self-merge, publish PATCH_SUMMARY

modules.label: deadline_reminder_loop — the T-45m and T-5m channel posts
the idle watchdog: 600 seconds, checked every 60
the delivery constraint the cutoff enforces

steps.narrative: The cycle repeats — claim, build, verify, merge, publish — under two kinds of central pressure that are code, not emergence: the runner's deadline posts at T-45 and T-5 minutes, which switch the team from coverage to landing, and the idle watchdog's DM nudges. At the cutoff the runner exports committed main HEAD; the grader builds it fresh from a clone, which is why the deadline posts insist that unmerged work does not count.
steps.representation:
channel pbench-task, from the runner:
  T-45m: "Stop dispatching new features... Land the
          open PRs; work that is not merged does not count."
  T-5m:  "Merge anything that is ready right now, then stop."
cutoff: export git HEAD of main -> fresh-clone build -> tests
steps.title: The loop repeats until the deadline posts land

title: One ProgramBench task, end to end — Agensh
